title: The Sunday schedule
body:
Every scheduler I talk to in assisted living and nursing tells me some version of the same story.

Sunday night. Kitchen table. Last week's Excel file open. Copying names across, fixing the three people who asked off, texting the two who still haven't answered.

Then Monday morning someone says, "I didn't know I was on."

The schedule isn't hard because scheduling is hard. It's hard because it lives in a spreadsheet, a group chat and someone's memory at the same time.

That's the problem we're solving with WiserShifts: build the week once, send it to everyone in one click, and let each person see just their shifts on their phone.

Schedulers: what part of your week takes the longest?

#SeniorLiving #Scheduling #NursingHomes
visual: A laptop with a spreadsheet at night, or just the line "I didn't know I was on."

title: Next week starts from this week
body:
Most weeks look a lot like last week.

Same people. Same shifts. A few time-off requests, a new hire, someone who switched to nights.

So why does every new schedule start from a blank page?

In WiserShifts, you set your weekly needs once: how many CNAs, med techs and nurses each shift needs. Every new week starts from that.

Then auto-fill keeps last week's people in the same spots and fills the gaps with whoever is free and qualified. You fix the few things that changed and send it.

Ten minutes instead of a Sunday.

#SeniorLivingOperations #Scheduling #AssistedLiving

title: Your staff don't need an app
body:
One decision we made early: staff don't download anything to see their schedule.

When a care facility rolls out a new app, half the CNAs install it, a quarter forget the password, and the scheduler ends up texting the schedule anyway.

So in WiserShifts, each person gets their own link by text or email. Tap it, see your shifts. If you have the app, it opens there. If not, it opens in the browser. No account. No password.

The scheduler gets one place to build and send. Staff get one link that always shows the current week.

Simple beats feature-rich when your team works 12-hour shifts.

#SeniorLiving #CNA #EmployeeScheduling

title: Publish one unit at a time
body:
Memory Care's schedule is done. Assisted Living is still waiting on two time-off answers.

Do you hold everything until it's all perfect, or send what's ready?

We built WiserShifts so you can do either. Send the whole week, or send just one part of it: one unit, or one role like med techs or dining.

The people on the finished part get their shifts today. The rest go out when they're ready. Nobody waits on someone else's unit.

Small feature. Big difference on a Thursday afternoon.

#SeniorLiving #MemoryCare #WorkforceScheduling

title: Scheduling goes beyond nursing
body:
Scheduling a senior living community isn't just nursing.

It's CNAs and caregivers. Med techs. Dining and kitchen. Housekeeping. Maintenance. Activities. Front desk. Drivers.

Different teams, different shifts, often different people building each part.

In WiserShifts, every role and every area lives on one week, and you can work on one part without touching the rest: fill just the kitchen, send just housekeeping, check just Memory Care.

One schedule for the whole building. Built one piece at a time.

#SeniorLivingOperations #AssistedLiving #Scheduling

title: The 5 a.m. call-out
body:
5:04 a.m. "Can't make it today."

Now the scheduler is scrolling contacts, texting five people one by one, and hoping someone says yes before shift change.

In WiserShifts, the open shift goes out by text to the people who are qualified and free. Staff can pick it up right from their own link, and the schedule updates for everyone.

No phone tree. No group chat with 40 people. No guessing who already said no.

Call-outs will always happen. Covering them shouldn't take an hour.

#SeniorLiving #CNA #StaffingShortage

title: What a call-out really costs
body:
Quick math most facilities never do.

One call-out on a 12-hour shift can mean overtime at time-and-a-half, or an agency CNA at a premium rate, plus the time someone spends finding a replacement.

Now multiply by how many call-outs you get in a month.

We built a free calculator so you can run it with your own numbers in two minutes.

wisershifts.com/calculators/call-out-cost-calculator?utm_source=linkedin

What number did you get? I'm curious how it compares across buildings.

title: A no-show isn't an open shift
body:
Something we just fixed, because a customer caught it.

Two people were scheduled. Neither clocked in. The shift ended, and the schedule showed two open spots for a shift that was already over.

That's wrong. You can't fill a shift that already happened.

Now a spot that's over shows what actually happened: the no-shows in red, and how many people you were short. Open spots only show for shifts you can still fill.

Small detail. But a schedule should tell the truth about yesterday, not just plan tomorrow.

#BuildInPublic #SeniorLiving #Scheduling
visual: Real screenshot of a past day on the week grid: names in red with "2 no-show" and "2 short".

title: Swaps without the group chat
body:
"Can anyone take my Saturday?" posted to a group chat of 40 people.

Twelve replies. Three people think they said yes. Nobody tells the scheduler.

With the holidays coming, this happens a lot.

In WiserShifts, staff ask a coworker to swap right from their own schedule link. When it goes through, the schedule updates for everyone, and the scheduler sees exactly who's working.

Let people trade. Just keep the schedule true.

#SeniorLiving #CNA #HolidayStaffing

title: Time off without the sticky note
body:
Where do time-off requests live at your building?

A sticky note on the monitor. A text from last Tuesday. A form in a folder. Someone's memory.

Then the schedule goes out and someone who asked off is on it.

In WiserShifts, staff request time off from their own link, and it shows up in one place for the scheduler to approve before the week is built.

One place to ask. One place to answer. No "but I told you."
